agree.reason: An investor who is already cold gets a clear, candid picture, but the apology has nothing behind it (no explanation, no promised schedule for updates, no January 7 date) and there is no specific ask, so it is unlikely to win back their trust or their willingness to keep taking calls.

honest.reason: Most claims are accurate, and the before-and-after caveat on reminders is a good touch, but "a quarter of new sales went to replacing lost revenue" has no basis in the facts given and contradicts flat MRR, which means all net new revenue went to replacing what was lost.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly works out the 11-month runway, the net gain of 5 clinics, the near-halving of no-shows and $1,500 per 10 reminder clinics, but it never shows how many reminder sales it would take to change the runway or reduce the $44K burn.

right_comparison.reason: It states the do-nothing path (11 months of cash, flat MRR, more customers could leave the same way), but it doesn't put a number on the churn risk or say what flat revenue means for the runway trend.

qualification.reason: "The coming quarter will show whether clinics will pay" names no target number, no date to check it against, and no consequence if the target is missed.

objections.reason: This investor's real objection is the silence and whether it will happen again, and the draft never answers it: no reason is given for the missed updates and no regular schedule is promised, and "thanks for your patience" reads badly to someone who complained about the silence.

fit.reason: It is a well-structured investor email of about 430 words with a clear subject line, which fits the 500-word limit and the 11-investor audience.
